questions.explain: The model gets only the relevant schema slice — top-5 tables by vector search over embedded descriptions plus columns; example_values per column eliminate the largest class of generation errors (date formats, enum casings, ID shapes).
options: Retrieved top-5 relevant tables with descriptions and example_values per column
The entire database schema in every prompt
No schema at all; the model guesses
questions.q: How is the model grounded on schema without blowing the context budget?

questions.explain: Five gates: parse (single SELECT), allowlist (known tables/columns), tenant filter (static analysis), cost guard via SET SHOWPLAN_XML estimated cost, and least-privilege execution as the final backstop.
options: Parse, allowlist, tenant filter, cost guard via estimated plan, least-privilege execution
questions.q: What are the five validation gates for generated SQL?

questions.explain: Temperature 0 makes generation deterministic — the same question produces the same query — which builds user trust and lets the validation cache key on the SQL text.
questions.q: Why does text-to-SQL generation use temperature 0?

questions.explain: Validated SQL is cached by SHA2_256 of the normalized question; schema migrations bump schema_version, invalidating stale SQL — repeat questions never pay generation cost twice.
options: Cache validated SQL by question hash; invalidate on schema_version bumps
questions.q: How is validated SQL cached and invalidated?

questions.explain: A second LLM call explains the SQL in two sentences for non-technical users, shown alongside results with a 'show SQL' toggle — the correction when the explanation reveals a misinterpretation is the highest-value feedback.
options: Explain the SQL in plain language alongside results, with a show-SQL toggle for power users
Never show the SQL to users
Explanations are a waste of tokens
questions.q: How does the chapter close the trust loop on generated SQL?
